top_level_objectives: Explain the chemical structure, directionality (5' and 3' ends), and antiparallel nature of the DNA double helix.
Demonstrate how complementary base pairing works via hydrogen bonding (A-T with two bonds, G-C with three).
Compare and contrast the molecular mechanisms of continuous leading strand synthesis and discontinuous lagging strand synthesis.
Formulate why the DNA replication process is classified as semiconservative using physical models of the daughter helices.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the three-dimensional double helix, focusing on the antiparallel directionality of the sugar-phosphate backbones.
key_visuals: A large, interactively rotatable 3D model of a DNA double helix.
Color-coded 5' (phosphate) and 3' (hydroxyl) ends of both strands.
An interactive magnification window showing the carbon numbering (1' through 5') on the deoxyribose sugar ring.
student_actions: Rotate and scale the DNA model to inspect the overall helical structure.
Tap on the 5' carbon and 3' carbon of a single nucleotide to trace the chemical directionality of the backbone.
Compare the directions of the two strands side-by-side to verify that they run antiparallel to each other.

scenes.brief_purpose: Investigate complementary base pairing, distinguishing between purines/pyrimidines and comparing hydrogen-bond configurations.
key_visuals: Close-up of nitrogenous bases projecting inward from the sugar-phosphate backbones.
Dotted lines indicating hydrogen bonds: two between Adenine and Thymine, and three between Guanine and Cytosine.
A side panel displaying base structures (purine double-rings vs. pyrimidine single-rings).
student_actions: Drag and match free nitrogenous bases (A, T, G, C) to their complementary template partners on an exposed single-strand section.
Observe and count the formation of hydrogen bonds (2 for A-T, 3 for G-C) when bases are correctly paired.
Identify and group bases as purines or pyrimidines based on their ring structures.

scenes.brief_purpose: Observe the initiation of DNA replication, including the unwinding of the helix and single-strand stabilization.
key_visuals: A replication fork where the double helix begins to separate.
A 3D model of the Helicase enzyme positioned at the junction of separation.
Single-strand binding proteins (SSBs) clustering on the newly exposed single-stranded templates.
student_actions: Drag Helicase along the double helix to actively break the hydrogen bonds and unzip the strands.
Place single-strand binding proteins onto the exposed single strands to prevent them from reannealing or forming secondary structures.
Identify the resulting replication fork and label the template strands with their 5'-to-3' orientations.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore continuous 5' to 3' synthesis on the leading strand by DNA polymerase.
key_visuals: The 3'-to-5' parental template strand running toward the replication fork.
DNA Polymerase III moving continuously in the direction of the unwinding replication fork.
Free dNTPs aligning and being chemically joined to the growing 3' end of the new strand.
student_actions: Trigger the synthesis of an RNA primer by RNA Primase to provide a free 3'-OH group.
Manually guide DNA Polymerase III along the leading strand toward the replication fork.
Select the correct incoming complementary dNTPs to synthesize the new continuous strand in the 5' to 3' direction.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine discontinuous synthesis on the lagging strand, highlighting the formation of Okazaki fragments.
key_visuals: The 5'-to-3' parental template strand running away from the replication fork.
RNA Primase laying down primers at interval sites.
DNA Polymerase III synthesizing short segments (Okazaki fragments) in the direction opposite to the fork movement.
student_actions: Place multiple RNA primers on the lagging template strand at appropriate intervals.
Initiate DNA Polymerase III to synthesize an Okazaki fragment from one primer to the next.
Analyze why this strand must be synthesized discontinuously due to the unidirectional constraint (5' to 3' synthesis) of the enzyme.

scenes.brief_purpose: Complete the replication process by replacing RNA primers, sealing nicks, and visualizing the semiconservative end product.
key_visuals: DNA Polymerase I replacing RNA primers with DNA nucleotides.
DNA Ligase sealing the nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone.
Two final DNA double helices, color-coded to show one parental template strand (original) and one newly synthesized strand in each molecule.
student_actions: Deploy DNA Polymerase I to excise and replace the RNA primers on the lagging strand.
Apply DNA Ligase to bond the Okazaki fragments together, creating a continuous backbone.
Inspect both finished double helices and identify the origin of each strand to conclude why the process is termed 'semiconservative'.
